correctness.rationale: The Euclidean digit recurrence is standard and was checked against the primary rational-base definition. Floor increments over each radix block have values 0 or 1 and exactly a jumps; opposite-parity phase changes give C(bN)=tN-C(aN). The count enumerates all aN input edges without duplication, and iterating the exact identity yields the logarithmic error. When both parameters are odd, strong induction proves alternation. Independent recursive and direct-digit finite computations match for 149 coprime bases and six long prefixes; finite tests do not substitute for the proof.

originality.rationale: A general all-coprime-rational-radix exact edge-count identity and logarithmic discrepancy follow from a new floor-jump parity argument. Rigo–Stipulanti characterizes rational-base automaticity and Dekking treats base 3/2 substitutions; the numerically reported 3/2 bigram law in Cassaigne et al. and a related indexed 3/2 variant run law are acknowledged. Actual semantic record and primary-source comparisons did not find the general quantified identity, although unindexed equivalents are possible.
residual_risks: An unindexed proof of the general floor-jump identity may exist in literature on rational-base digit sums or block substitutions.
The full exhaustive bibliography of adjacent statistics in all rational bases was not available; the literature search is nonexhaustive.
Individual frequencies of 00 and 11 in arbitrary rational bases are outside this claim.

value.rationale: A complete, exact natural two-point invariant simultaneously for all coprime rational bases extends the hard individual 3/2 work. It exhibits the structural even-parameter/(a+b) universality, a distinct all-odd alternating branch, and a rigorous O(log N) discrepancy. This is an infinite family theorem, rather than an arbitrary finite enumeration or routine restatement of an individual frequency.
